Posterior transition matrix of a VAR trend

Source: R/var_param_extractors.R
posterior_transition_matrix.Rd

The coefficient matrix \(A_l\) of lag \(l\) of a VAR() trend. Row \(i\) holds the effects of the processes at time \(t - l\) on process \(i\) at time \(t\). The diagonal holds each process's persistence. The off-diagonal cells hold the effects of one process on another.

Usage

posterior_transition_matrix(
  object,
  groups = NULL,
  summary = TRUE,
  robust = FALSE,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  lag = 1L
)

Arguments

object

A fitted mvgam object whose trend is a VAR.

groups

The panels of a hierarchical VAR, by level or by index, or "all". NULL gives the mean of the panels' matrices. A single-panel fit takes NULL alone. One panel returns its matrix. Several, or "all", return a list whose plot() method is plot.mvgam_var_matrix_list().

summary

Logical. TRUE returns the summary of each cell. FALSE returns the draws as a [ndraws, K, K] array, with the processes naming its second and third dimensions.

robust

Logical. If FALSE (the default), uses mean and standard deviation for summaries. If TRUE, uses median and median absolute deviation (MAD).

probs

Numeric vector of probabilities for quantile computation. Default is c(0.025, 0.975) for 95% credible intervals. Can be a single value or multiple values.

lag

The lag of the matrix, at most the order p of the fitted VAR(p).

Value

With summary = TRUE, an mvgam_var_matrix: a list of the matrices A, A_se, A_lower, A_upper, A_ess, prob_positive, prob_negative and prob_nonzero, with n_series, series_names, group_label, probs and lag. It has print() and plot() methods. With summary = FALSE, the array of draws. Several panels give a list of either.

Details

A hierarchical VAR (VAR(gr = ...)) has one matrix per panel. groups names a panel to return its matrix. With groups = NULL the function returns the mean of the panels' matrices, computed in each draw. The hyperparameters Amu_trend and Aomega_trend pool unconstrained matrices, which the stationarity map of Heaps (2023) turns into each panel's matrix. Their mean is no transition matrix. The mean over panels summarises the pool on the scale of the matrices.

Each cell is summarised as residual_cor() summarises a correlation. The estimate is the posterior mean, or the median with robust = TRUE. The interval takes the quantiles probs. The effective sample size comes from posterior::ess_basic(). prob_positive, prob_negative and prob_nonzero are the shares of draws above zero, below zero and away from zero.

References

Savage J (2016). Hierarchical Vector Autoregression. RPubs, 27 November 2016. https://rpubs.com/jimsavage/hierarchical_var

Heaps SE (2023). Enforcing stationarity through the prior in vector autoregressions. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics 32(1), 74-83. doi:10.1080/10618600.2022.2079648

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(0)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = gaussian(), n_series = 3L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = VAR(),
                    prop_trend = 0.95)
var_mod <- mvgam(y ~ 1, trend_formula = ~ VAR(p = 1),
                 data = simdat$data_train, family = gaussian(),
                 chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 3 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 1 of 2 chains had an E-BFMI less than 0.3.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# Each series' persistence and its effects on the others
A <- posterior_transition_matrix(var_mod)
A
#> Lag-1 VAR transition matrix from an mvgam fit
#>   Group      : single-panel
#>   Dimension  : 3 x 3
#>   Mean |A_ij| (i != j): 0.12
#>   Point estimate:
#>          series_1 series_2 series_3
#> series_1     0.68     0.03     0.14
#> series_2     0.08     0.53     0.21
#> series_3     0.17     0.08     0.56
#>   95% CI on each cell available in `A_lower` / `A_upper`.
plot(A)


# Next, irf(var_mod) traces how a shock to one series spreads
# }
